scope: READINESS AUDIT ONLY. Nothing was retired, no production was polled or mutated, no migration script was run, no legacy code was removed, no finding state was changed.
headline: NOT READY — and the blocker is larger than the frontend. The canonical conversation read path shares NO storage with the legacy stacks and there is NO compatibility layer, so legacy history is reachable only through legacy surfaces until a manual, deploy-independent migration is run. Separately, eleven backend files still produce `/me/correspondence/...` deep links, which are already persisted in production notification and activity rows.

prerequisite2_historyMigration.status: NOT COMPLETE (as far as structure can prove) — UNKNOWN against production, and the evidence needed is exact
prerequisite2_historyMigration.exactMeaning: A DATA migration, not a schema migration. scripts/migrate-conversations.js copies two legacy stacks into the canonical tables: (1) DirectThread + DirectMessage -> Conversation + ConversationMessage, with dual attribution mapped 1:1 (actorType/actorInstitutionId -> speakingForInstitutionId), read cursors -> ConversationHumanState, archive flags -> archivedAt; (2) personal Spaces (PRIVATE 1:1s and the two named personal spaces) holding EXACTLY ONE thread -> one Conversation each, the human-chosen title becoming the Conversation name as presentation only, members -> plain parties (roles do not survive), per-member state -> ConversationHumanState.

properties.idempotent: YES, by construction — deterministic primary keys derived from legacy ids ('dt:<threadId>', 'sp:<spaceId>', 'dm:<msgId>', 'm:<msgId>') with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING throughout. Re-running inserts zero rows.
properties.nonDestructive: YES — reads legacy tables, writes ONLY the new tables. The script's own header states legacy deletion is a separately authorized later phase.
properties.directKeyPolicy: A migrated pair claims the canonical directKey only if the canonical system has not already created one for that pair; new-system rows win and the migrated row then carries history without pair identity, reported for review. PRIVATE spaces with more than 2 ACTIVE members migrate WITHOUT directKey.
properties.skipRule: A personal space with zero or more than one thread is SKIPPED and REPORTED. At §62 measurement time none existed.

isItRunByDeploy.answer: NO — and this is the decisive structural fact.
isItRunByDeploy.evidence: scripts/railway-start.sh runs exactly two stages: `npx prisma migrate deploy` then `node dist/src/main.js`. It never invokes migrate-conversations.js or seed-public-spaces.js, and nothing else in the repo references either script. The 2026-08-20 production logs corroborate it: 'No pending migrations to apply' — the Prisma stage, not the history migration.
isItRunByDeploy.consequence: Pushing and deploying — which happened on 2026-08-19/20 — does NOT advance this prerequisite. The §62 phrase 'run through the authorized deployment path' must mean a founder-run step, because the deployment path as coded does not contain it.

compatibilityLayer.evidence: ConversationsService touches no legacy table. There is no adapter that reads DirectThread/Space and presents it as a Conversation. Legacy and canonical are separate storage.
compatibilityLayer.consequence: History is NOT visible through the canonical surface until the rows are physically copied. Until then, every legacy conversation is reachable ONLY through legacy code.

If the legacy family were removed before the migration runs and is verified, every DirectThread and personal-space conversation in production becomes unreachable — the data would still be in the database, with no code able to read it.

readOnlyEvidenceOwed.why: Whether the migration has already been run manually cannot be determined from the repository. It can only be read from production, and this audit does not poll production.
readOnlyEvidenceOwed.note: `node scripts/migrate-conversations.js --dry-run` is NOT sufficient on its own: the dry-run branch returns before the VERIFICATION block, so it reports the legacy corpus only and never compares it to what has been migrated. Recorded because reaching for --dry-run is the obvious move and it would answer the wrong question.
readOnlyEvidenceOwed.exactReadOnlyQuery: SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "DirectThread") AS legacy_dt, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "Conversation" WHERE id LIKE 'dt:%') AS migrated_dt, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "DirectMessage") AS legacy_dm, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "ConversationMessage" WHERE id LIKE 'dm:%') AS migrated_dm, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "Space" s WHERE s."institutionId" IS NULL AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "Thread" t2 WHERE t2."spaceId"=s.id) = 1) AS legacy_sp, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "Conversation" WHERE id LIKE 'sp:%') AS migrated_sp;
readOnlyEvidenceOwed.interpretation: All migrated_* zero => migration never run. migrated_* equal to legacy_* => complete. Anything between => partial, and the skipped-space report matters.
readOnlyEvidenceOwed.baselineToCompareAgainst: §62 read-only measurement (2026-08-16): 5 DirectThreads / 9 messages; 10 PRIVATE personal spaces / 67 messages; 0 grown-past-pair; 2 named personal spaces ('family' CIRCLE 2 members/3 msgs, 'Aura Internal' WORKROOM 3 members/1 msg). Production has moved since; treat as a floor, not a target.

rollbackRecovery.isRetirementCodeOnly: YES as scoped — Phase 5 removes screens, routes, modules and adapters. It deletes no data. The migration itself is additive and non-destructive.
rollbackRecovery.isRevertSufficient: YES for the code deletion: a git revert restores the legacy surfaces and routes, and the legacy DATA is untouched and still present, so restored code finds its rows exactly where it left them.
rollbackRecovery.irreversibleSteps: NONE identified. The migration is idempotent and additive; re-running it inserts zero rows. Nothing in Phase 5 as scoped destroys anything.
rollbackRecovery.theRealRisk: Not data loss but ADDRESS loss — persisted deep links pointing at deleted routes. A revert restores those routes, so it is recoverable, but it is the failure most likely to be noticed by users first.
rollbackRecovery.compatibilityPathForOneRelease: NOT designed and NOT recommended by default. If the founder wants persisted deep links to keep working after retirement, the cheap option is a redirect from /me/correspondence/... to the canonical conversation rather than retaining the legacy runtime. Flagged as a decision, not built.

authorizationThreshold: READY FOR FOUNDER RETIREMENT AUTHORIZATION requires ALL of: (1) the history migration has been run against production and verified by the migrated-vs-legacy counts, with the skipped-space report empty or explicitly dispositioned; (2) no conversation, message, participant, attachment or read cursor exists only in legacy storage; (3) backend deep-link production emits the canonical conversation route, and persisted legacy deep links either resolve or are deliberately accepted as broken by founder ruling; (4) the frontend communication resolver and route normalizer target canonical routes; (5) correspondence_identity.dart's two live consumers have been moved off it, so deletion discharges all 7 of its identity sites; (6) journeys J1-J10 observed and certified, with J11 either passing or explicitly waived; (7) conversations_screen has an FD-12 proven-dead disposition; (8) the retirement manifest is executed as REMOVE-only with no data deletion; (9) rollback is a plain git revert with legacy data intact. None of these may be assumed from clean local code.
